# rigid-dynamics.library: ApplyGravityAndDamping

**Status:** Experimental (tier `future`). Aspirational vocabulary. It must parse and type-check; it is not linted or converted to C#.

## Summary

> The world with gravity and damping applied to every body's velocity, and no
> other wrench. A caller with per-body forces calls `IntegrateVelocity` itself
> with the wrench it assembled; this is the free-fall case, which is the one a
> scene without actuators is in.

### Line 831

**Source:** [stdlib/future/rigid-dynamics.library.plato, line 831](../../../../../stdlib/future/rigid-dynamics.library.plato#L831).

```plato

    //==
    // # The step
    //
    // One fixed step, as a pure function of the world. The order is forced:
    // velocities must be final before positions move (semi-implicit Euler), and
    // contacts must be solved before that, or the step would move bodies through
    // each other and solve the interpenetration next frame.

    // The world with gravity and damping applied to every body's velocity, and no
    // other wrench. A caller with per-body forces calls `IntegrateVelocity` itself
    // with the wrench it assembled; this is the free-fall case, which is the one a
    // scene without actuators is in.
    ApplyGravityAndDamping(world: RigidWorld3D): RigidWorld3D
    {
        var seconds = world.TimeStep.FixedDeltaTime.Seconds;
        var free = SpatialForce3D(Vector3D.Zero, Vector3D.Zero);
        return RigidWorld3D(
            world.Bodies.Map(body => IntegrateVelocity(body, free, world.Gravity, seconds)),
            world.Constraints,
            world.Gravity,
            world.TimeStep,
            world.Solver);
    }
```
